reflections.title: "Blessed in the City and the Country"

reflect.text: Moses placed a serious choice before God's people between covenant blessing and judgment. God's promises of provision are conditional rather than automatic, touching our families and daily labor. We are constantly vulnerable to temptation, and assuming we could never stumble is a dangerous mistake. Yet as Alistair Begg reminds us, Christ bore the curse of our disobedience so that we could receive His gifts.

Because of this grace, God's favor reaches us wherever we live. A crowded city is full of noise, hurry, and daily worries. Walking with God takes the sharp edge off those struggles. His blessing may not make us wealthy, but it keeps us upright and gives us useful work among the crowds. When we feel we are waiting on God to act, He may simply be waiting for our willing obedience.

The quiet country receives this same blessing. God meets us when we walk alone in the fields to pray, just as He met Isaac in the evening. He prospers the hard labor of the plow and harvest. He blesses our outdoor exercise and our study of nature, and He remains our comfort even when we visit the ground where we bury our dead.

questions: In what part of your daily routine, whether busy or quiet, do you most need God's presence today?
Is there an area of your life where God is waiting for you to obey Him before moving forward?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for sending Jesus to take the curse for our sins so we could know Your kindness. Guide our steps whether we are among crowded streets or in quiet fields. Give us willing hearts to hear Your voice and walk in Your truth today. Amen.

reflections.title: The Bounty of Walking with God

reflect.text: Receiving God's bounty is tied to hearing and following His word, though having material goods does not always mean God approves of our spiritual state. God promises to bless our daily food as well as what we store up. Whether we have just enough food for today or savings set aside, we need His help so that wealth does not turn into an idol that hardens our hearts. Victory over greed and sin comes through the Holy Spirit rather than our own resolve.

The Lord also blesses us when we come in and when we go out. We can inspect our private souls and home duties in peace, and then step outside into the world to help others and stand for what is right. God opens His heavenly storehouse to supply us, pouring out His refreshing spiritual gifts just like rain in its season. He invites every believer to ask and receive the rich treasures found in Christ.

Finally, God calls His people to lead the way rather than follow behind like a tail tossed around by worldly habits. When we belong to the Lord, we do not need to tremble before anyone. God's mighty protection surrounds us, giving us courage to stand up for the truth without fear.

questions: How can you honor God with the things He has placed in your care, whether small daily meals or larger savings?
Are you letting popular opinion pull you along, or are you leading the way with quiet Christian courage?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, bless the work of our hands and keep our hearts free from the love of money. Open Your heavenly storehouse to refresh our spirits each day. Make us bold to follow You faithfully without fear of what others may say. Amen.
